newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: MOLDOVAN PARLIAMENT ELECTED NEW CHAIRMAN.
newsitem.headline: MOLDOVAN PARLIAMENT ELECTED NEW CHAIRMAN.

text.p: Moldovan parliament, in a move to reject accusations of inefficiency and conservatism, on Wednesday elected new chairman and committed itself to adopt legislation, which would push reforms.

Dumitru Motpan, leader of the ruling Agrarian-democratic party and former deputy speaker, was elected chairman of the parliament by 55 votes for and 21 against, only two votes over the necessary simple majority of 53.

The parliament failed to elect new chairman for over two months after the former speaker, Petru Lucinschi, was elected Moldova's president in December poll. Supporters of Motpan's rival, another deputy speaker Dumitru Diacov, blocked the election.
The parliament was criticized by the opposition and the media for being unable to work and adopt legislation.
Lucinschi welcomed election of the parliament's chairman and called the deputies not to turn the legislative body into "a battlefield of empty ambitions" and "an obstacle in the way of reforms".
"So far, our successes were more declarative.
We found ourselves in a new stagnation... Reforms in Moldova should be accelerated", Lucinschi said in an adress to the parliament.
Lucinschi named about 40 draft laws the

parliament should adopt in order to create legislative framework for reforms. They include 1997 budget, 1997-1998 privatisation programme, Tax, Land and Civil Codes, laws on non-public pension funds and combating organized crime.
Lucinschi proposed to the political parties, including the opposition, to sign a Pact, which would set up a framework for cooperation between different political forces in Moldova.
"The president singled out the most important tasks to be tackled by the parliament. The budget is the most urgent one", Motpan said.

New chairman of the Moldovan parliament is 56 years old. He graduated from agricultural college and higher communist party school. Before being elected to the previous parliament in 1989 he headed a collective farm. In 1994 Motpan was realected to the new parliament and became its deputy chairman. REUTER
